name: Starfall run messages
summary: The Starfall card shows for only the first 1.6s - "STARFALL / Catch the stars / You're safe. Stars score double." - then a two-second STARFALL COMPLETE result card.
detail: The countdown tag, the "Red is cleared" wording and the progress bar recorded here previously were replaced at commit 01a3a25 by a single opening card that returns null after 1.6s, leaving the arena uncaptioned for the rest of the release. The arming state still prints STARFALL EARNED / The stars are coming / Keep flying, and the header prints "STARFALL n / N ORBITS" while charging - never in the lab, in a black hole or during Starfall itself. dropNeed() is 3, or 2 with EARLY STARFALL.

name: SWIPE CONTROLS chooser
summary: A live-arena screen titled SWIPE CONTROLS with the sub 'Swipe to try them. Both work.', two rows and CONFIRM, teaching the two hop rules by letting the player feel them.
detail: Rows: 'Up / down' - 'Outward is always up' (screen) and 'Toward / away' - 'Outward is away from the center' (radial). An arrow at the comet shows where the selected rule says out is right now: pinned upward under the screen rule, rotating with the comet under the radial one. Reachable only from the title screen's Swipe controls row or via the lab door on a device that never chose - a fresh device is defaulted to 'screen' by beginIntro instead. Every telemetry event carries swipe_mode.

radialRow: Outward is away from the center

name: lesson_shown / card_shown
summary: Teaching has its own funnel: flushLesson emits lesson_shown when a lesson ends (including cut short by a death), and cardDone emits card_shown.
detail: lesson_shown carries type, soft, rearmed, age, game_level, run_index and cut. card_shown carries game_level, after_clear, seconds and run_index. run_ended additionally carries killer_lesson_seen, killer_relessoned, lessons_shown, did_hop, death_cause and hold_timeout. Without the cut flush, exactly the lessons interrupted by the death they should have prevented vanished from the funnel. Telemetry is suppressed wholesale for lab runs.

name: title screen
summary: The title screen has no how-to key any more: logo, 'Move with the music.', an optional BEST line, LAUNCH, POWER-UP LAB, SIGN IN/LEADERBOARD, Swipe controls and Learn to play.
detail: docs/design/teaching.md's 'The menu key is four rows, not nine' and MECHANICS.md's 'four-row key' describe a block that no longer exists; the verbs are taught by the demo comet and by FIRST FLIGHT instead. 'Swipe controls' clears G.swipeAsked and reopens the chooser; 'Learn to play' calls beginIntro(). A tap on the background still starts a run.

name: black-hole guarantee scope
summary: Level 4 guarantees the black hole is OFFERED once per run, not taken: bhPlaced marks the offer spent and a decline arms a 20s cooldown, after which only the ordinary 5% roll remains.
detail: The guarantee branch requires level>=4, !bhRun, !bhPlaced, G.t>=G.bhCool and !bhActive(). Placing it sets bhPlaced, bhRun and bhCool=G.t+20. bhRun is cleared only when carried is false - a genuinely fresh run, not a level advance - which is what makes the guarantee once per run rather than once per level. Unlike every other orb it is a real choice with a cost either way, so a guarantee to OFFER is the only kind it can carry.

name: what survives a level boundary
summary: startGame() runs at every level advance as well as every fresh run, and `carried` is the one switch deciding whether score, journey, guarantees, first-time flags and the intro trio reset.
detail: Kept when carried: the score - restored, with the layer ladder seeded from it - the sky journey G.skyW, orbits/lands/bestStreak/bestGroove, bhRun, the six orb-guarantee flags, didReverse/didHop/didLap, saidChor and introN. Cleared regardless: G.tier and G.nRings before the pre-climb, the board, the shield bank, groove and build state, PAUSE, chorusN/chorusBars and the started clock - so per-level and per-run are two different scopes inside one function. G.runs++ also fires here, so run_index advances at every level boundary.

name: the level card
summary: State lvend draws the level card: a level number and name, then either three upgrade tiles on a real advance or a one-line tip and a LEVEL n button on a retry or a picked start.
detail: Three entries: levelComplete() sets {done:true,next:level+1} and calls rollOffer(); retry() sets {done:false,next:G.level} for level 2+; startFromSelect() sets {done:false,next:n} when the device has no runs yet or n>=2. cardDone() commits G.level and reports card_shown with the seconds it was read. A level-1 retry, and a level-1 start by a player who has run before, skip the card entirely.

name: LV[].mech (mostly dead)
summary: LV[].mech has one reader: the card's tip line reads mech[0][1] only, and only for levels 2-6, so level 1's three rows and every level's rows past the first never render.
detail: The only read is const tip = n===1 ? 'Learn the controls as you play.' : (L.mech[0]&&L.mech[0][1]) || ... . Level 1's card substitutes a hardcoded string, so its ['swipe',null] row - annotated 'resolved at draw time by swipeWords()' - is never resolved by anything. That tip is also the else branch of `offered`, so on a real level advance the upgrade tiles take the slot and no mech line shows at all. The comment above LV says the card lines are checked against MECHANICS.md; check.mjs's ledger guard reads TIERS and LAB_ORBS names only.

name: carried = !!G.carryScore
summary: The level-boundary signal is a score, not a flag: startGame reads const carried=!!G.carryScore, so a clear banked with a zero score would be handled as a fresh run.
detail: The line is read directly at src/game/runtime.js:6136; the consequence is reasoned. levelComplete() sets G.carryScore=G.score, and every carry decision downstream - journey, guarantee flags, didHop, introN, bhRun, the chorus naming line - keys off the truthiness of that number. A run that reached a finish line having scored nothing would therefore re-arm the whole beginner path on the next level. The star dive pays before levelComplete, so the only reachable route is the no-WebAudio path, which completes bare at the finish line with no dive.

name: dl() per-level rebase
summary: dl() returns the level's own dl0 plus a ramp re-run from zero at every level, so difficulty-seconds are absolute across the game but the gentle opening repeats per level.
detail: base = LV[G.level-1].dl0; the age term is (age()+min(G.diff*0.22,40))*MD().clock, and the first 80 seconds of each level advance at 0.55 rate before switching to 44+(a-80). So a level-4 start is dl 340 on its first frame, and the nudge good play earns is capped at 40. In the lab dl() is pinned to LAB_DL=40, chosen because it is exactly TIERS[3].at (THIRD RING) - three orbits - and level 1's finish line at 90 is then unreachable.

name: level prose vs source
summary: Where the level docs and the runtime's own comments disagree with LV and TIERS - the stale halves are listed in the note, and source wins in every case.
detail: Live at this commit: LEVEL_HOME's inline comment names VEIL for index 2 where WORLDS[2] is DUSTLANE; MECHANICS.md's claim that check.mjs reads level 2's finish line as ends[1] describes code that no longer exists; two runtime comments still describe the pre-six-level ladder; and docs/design/levels.md's unlock table quotes an older generation of every banner sentence, including the two rungs renamed to SHUTTERS and SHUTTER PAIRS.

name: EVENT HORIZON
summary: Level 4, dl 340-470: DIVERS at dl 395 - the first formation taught above dl 340 - plus the black hole's one guaranteed offer and THE MIRROR; opens on world GLASS.
detail: LV row 4. It was the endless level and now has a finish line; it keeps its identity as the black hole's level. dl 340 is also the floor every late-board rule is gated at: the SHAPE_RANK weighting ramp, the two-pair twin ceiling and the gap-floor decay all start here, so levels 1-3 are untouched by construction rather than by inspection.

name: level finish line and the star dive
summary: A level ends by latching the finale 10 dl-seconds early at a quiet musical moment and laying 11 trail stars plus a sun; with no WebAudio it completes bare at the finish line instead.
detail: Guarded by lvEnd<1e9 and !bhActive(). The latch needs no live finale, no starfall, dl()>=lvEnd-10 and a quiet payoff (MU.pay<=0 && !MU.rise). The trail is 11 stars 0.55 rad apart walking the cadence [4,3,2,4,3,2,1,3,2,1,0], four on the outer ring, four mid, three inner; the sun sits one step further and only blooms once the melody is nearly gathered, so the ending is always a deliberate dive. levelComplete() rolls the upgrade offer, banks carryScore/orbits/lands/streak/groove/time and fires level_cleared.

name: HEAT DEATH
summary: Level 6, dl 610 onward with end:Infinity: THE EYE opens it, nothing new is taught, and the Infinity end is what makes the finale block skip it entirely.
detail: LV row 6. The finale latch is guarded by lvEnd<1e9, so an Infinity end means no star dive and no level completion - play simply continues. The owner retired the rule that the last level must stay endless; the comment beside the row calls Infinity a placeholder until the next level is built, not an endless-mode rule.

name: LEVEL_HOME
summary: Each level floors the sky journey at its own world - [0,1,2,3,4,7] into WORLDS - so a level never sends a travelling player backwards and every level has a distinct opening image.
detail: Applied as G.skyW=Math.max(G.skyW,LEVEL_HOME[...]) in startGame, and the journey itself survives a level boundary - only a fresh run zeroes G.skyW. VEIL (index 5) and GRID (6) are deliberately not homes: they are travelled through between REDSHIFT and HEAT DEATH by orbiting. The inline comment beside the array names VEIL for index 2, which is wrong - WORLDS[2] is DUSTLANE.

name: INTO THE RINGS
summary: Level 2, dl 90-215: the ring threats, unlocking GATES (100), DRIFTERS (128) and SHUTTERS (165); guarantees hypernova and slipstream; opens on world TIDE.
detail: LV row 2. Its card is two lines that say what the level IS - the earlier card previewed gates, drifters and shutters at dl 90, up to 75 seconds before the first one existed. The hypernova is the first post-curriculum placement (G.hyperPlaced) and slipstream follows it; both are once per RUN and pre-spent for a run that opens past level 2.

name: LIFT OFF
summary: Level 1, dl 0-90: the two verbs and the shard, unlocking SECOND RING (dl 12), TWIN SHARDS (18) and THIRD RING (40); opens on world DRIFT.
detail: LV row 1. key:1 is the reference key every other level's ratio is measured against. Guarantees here are the POW_INTRO trio shield->slow-mo->nova, ordered and once per run (G.introN). Its finish line at dl 90 runs the star dive; a first-ever run passes through its card, a returning player's level-1 start and retry are instant.

name: per-level orb guarantees
summary: spawnPow() is an ordered if-chain of level gates: hypernova and slipstream from level 2, magnet and star trail from 3, the mirror and the black hole offer from 4, scorch from 5.
detail: Order: lab override, the POW_INTRO trio, the pity shield at sinceShield>=3, the level-4 black hole guarantee, the 5% black hole roll from level 3, then hyper, mirror, scorch, spot, slip, trail, then the POWPOOL roll. Each guarantee is once per RUN - the flags survive level boundaries and are pre-spent for any home level behind the level a run opens on. The fallback roll respects the same level floors and renormalises over the eligible rows, so a first run on LIFT OFF cannot be handed the magnet.

name: the level picker and G.startLevel
summary: From the second run on, a picker offers all six levels; the choice is never persisted and G.startLevel>1 disables the deepest-level record and tags the share text.
detail: startFromSelect() clamps to LEVEL_MAX, sets G.level and G.startLevel, clears the upgrade state and every carry counter, then shows the level's card - or starts instantly at level 1 for a device that has runs. Rows the device has reached are marked Reached via G.lvlMax. G.newLevel, which drives FURTHEST YET and the cometloop:gl write, requires !LAB.on && G.startLevel===1, so a picked run can never move the record; the share text adds ' - from Ln' when startLevel>1.

name: silent tier pre-climb at a level start
summary: A level-2+ start (and the lab) sets G.tier=tierIndex() and raises G.nRings from the tiers below it before the first frame, so no banner fires for rungs the level opens past.
detail: Two lines: G.tier=tierIndex() and a loop taking the max of TIERS[i].rings for i<=tier. The card is the announcement instead. The same two lines give the lab its three rings from LAB_DL. tierIndex()'s twin hold is exempted for level>=2 by the level rather than by forging didHop, so the hop hint, the rehearsal and the death coach stay honest about what this run's thumbs actually did. skyI is recomputed by the same formula the in-run ratchet uses, clamped to the four sky bands.

name: REDSHIFT
summary: Level 5, dl 470-610: THE NARROWS at dl 520 and scorch; its own end (610) is what warnTime() reads as the endless level's floor.
detail: LV row 5. THE NARROWS is the last thing the game teaches and the mirror of GATES - one wall each for the two verbs, 420 difficulty-seconds apart. warnTime() derives examDl as LV[LEVEL_MAX-2].end rather than a literal, which is what moved the telegraph decay out of this teaching level and into HEAT DEATH.

name: LV
summary: The six-row level table: each row is {dl0, end, name, key, mech}, and LEVEL_MAX is LV.length rather than a literal.
detail: Windows are dl 0/90/215/340/470/610 with end:Infinity on the sixth. key is a frequency ratio (1, 0.8909, 0.7937, 0.7071, 0.6300, 0.5612) that scales the SFX pentatonic. LEVEL_MAX is declared immediately after the table so loadPrefs can clamp cometloop:gl against it. check.mjs asserts finish lines strictly increase; smoke.mjs asserts LEVEL_MAX===LV.length.

name: THE STORM
summary: Level 3, dl 215-340: the two compounds and the saucer, unlocking SLIDING GATES (240), THE SAUCER (275) and SHUTTER PAIRS (310); guarantees magnet and star trail.
detail: LV row 3. Three shapes ~35 dl apart, the spacing level 2 already used; the shutter pair moved 295->310 to keep it. The saucer's slot is the last one with room for its lesson, because a tier banner may not fire inside a level's endgame window. Level 3 is also the floor for the black hole's ordinary 5% roll.

name: G.tier vs G.level
summary: Two ordinals: G.tier is the thirteen-rung unlock ladder and speaks only through banners and telemetry; G.level is the 1-6 structure and owns every string the player reads.
detail: levelName() returns LV[G.level-1].name and feeds the HUD standing line, the death-screen subtitle and the share text. tierLabel() walks back to the nearest named rung and is read by telemetry only. runSummary() prints LEVEL n/LEVEL_MAX with one pip per level, filled to the level this run reached. The rule exists because the header once read LEVEL 4 next to a tier name seconds after the card said EVENT HORIZON: an earlier session tried to fix that by renaming the tier, and the collision came back one level later, because the defect was printing two ladders side by side.

name: Score-bought band layers
summary: Crossing 600, 1400, 2400 and 3600 points adds an accompaniment layer and says which one joined: RHYTHM, MELODY, DEEP BASS, HIGH NOTES.
detail: The announcement is queued at priority 2, not the queue minimum, because a bought layer is a reward and at priority 1 it lost the slot to every routine line for the whole 2.8s pump. startGame seeds G.layerN from the carried score so a level-2 start cannot print a false NEW MUSIC. The say line renders under the tag NEW MUSIC in the message card.

name: Band meter
summary: The standing dot row that showed which accompaniment layers were live is removed; musical growth is heard, not metered.
detail: The ledger keeps the row so a later session does not re-propose the HUD element: the arena HUD now prioritises score, level progress, shields and active powers, and the layer ladder announces itself once per crossing instead of holding permanent screen space. G.bandCap/G.bandCapT survive in the state object as the meter caption moment.

name: Black hole
summary: An optional three-act wager from level 3: opening warp, inner-ring charge, then an escape to the outer ring before 17s, paid on charge and stars.
detail: A fourth ring opens over 0.85s, motion settles at 0.60x and density ramps 1.25x to 2x; settled innermost travel banks dt/8 of charge and inner stars pay double. Gravity releases at 12s and the payout is round((80 + 600*charge + 20*stars) / 1.5^min(3,shieldsSpent)). Guaranteed to be OFFERED once per run from level 4, plus a 5% roll from level 3; taking one arms a 55s cooldown and declining costs 20s.

name: The chorus
summary: Each world carries a second progression that sustained engagement opens at a phrase boundary, and cooling off returns to the verse - no instruction anywhere.
detail: The section holds for CHOR_HOLD = 12 bars before it can fall back, and the switch is decided on a bar line rather than on the frame the heat crossed. It changes the soundtrack automatically and never requests a new action, which is why the ledger names the music itself as its only explanation.

name: Combo
summary: Consecutively collected stars pay one more each up to a cap of 6, inside a 2.5-second window, and the lesson fires at the third.
detail: G.combo = Math.min(G.combo+1, 6) with G.comboT = CW (2.5s). MEET.combo names the ceiling - "up to 6 points each" - because the earlier wording promised an unbounded climb three rungs before it flattened. The HUD chip prints COMBO xN so the counter and the lesson share a noun.

name: Difficulty clock
summary: dl() is difficulty-seconds: run age plus a capped nudge from scoring, re-based at every level floor, and every pressure term in the game reads it.
detail: dl() = LV[level-1].dl0 + ramp((age + min(G.diff*0.22, 40)) * mode.clock), where the ramp is a*0.55 below 80 and 44+(a-80) above. The intro returns 0 and the lab pins it to LAB_DL. Because speed, shard cap, arrival gap, warn length, the tier ladder and the finish line all key off this one number, a mode changes how many real seconds a rung costs and never which rung.

name: Divers
summary: The only shard that changes ring: it telegraphs on one orbit and 55% of the way through its warning transfers to an adjacent one, dl 395.
detail: The remaining 45% of the warn is the lesson - where it lands is where it kills, and you were shown, by a chevron sitting on the destination for the whole telegraph. Both the lane it leaves and the lane it lands in must be clear at placement or the spawn is rejected outright. It never rolls below two rings, since it needs somewhere to dive to.

values.lesson: It moves to the marked ring; swipe to another ring

name: Drifters
summary: Shards that slide along their own ring at one fixed random heading well under player speed at dl 128; they never steer and never chase.
detail: The spawn gives each a constant va and nothing updates it, which is why both drifter channels stopped saying "these ones chase you" and "keep moving" - the first named a behaviour the player would watch not happen and the second named an action the game does not have. The lesson names the input instead: tap to turn away.

values.lesson: This red obstacle moves; tap to turn away

name: Automatic drum fill
summary: The accompaniment plays an authored eight-step fill on an earned arrangement change; player inputs are never remapped to drums.
detail: MU.brk is armed on a bar line with a 30-second cooldown and counts down to MU.brkEnd. During a break the hop pushes a deep gold ring and the reverse a white flash, so the fill is visible with the sound off. There is no instruction channel for it at all, by design - the ledger names the music itself as its only explanation.

name: Gates
summary: One angle blocked on every ring at dl 100, so hopping cannot save you and the answer is the tap; vetted at spawn for a 1.1 rad reversal.
detail: spawnSpike downgrades a gate to a plain single if reverseEscape(GATE_ESCAPE) cannot find 1.1 radians of clear run behind the player, so the formation that demands a reversal can never be placed where a reversal is impossible. While a wall is live the placement bubble goes symmetric, and no gate may share a board with another wall or with the saucer.

values.lesson: A wall blocks every ring; tap to turn around

name: Hop (swipe)
summary: A swipe moves the comet one ring in or out under whichever of the two swipe rules the device chose, and every hop instruction is worded from that rule at draw time.
detail: swipeOut() is the only expression of either rule: screen mode returns dy<0, radial mode returns dx*cos(ang)+dy*sin(ang)*AY>0. swipeWords() supplies the sentence, so the SECOND RING banner, the hint rung, the intro step and the death coach cannot describe a rule the build does not have. A swipe past the last ring bumps, plays a free note and costs nothing. hop() persists cometloop:hopped outside the lab, which is what gates the once-ever rehearsal.

values.screenWords: swipe up or down to change ring
values.radialWords: swipe out or in to change ring

name: Hypernova (pink star)
summary: Sixteen beats of invincibility at up to 1.9x speed where red converts to paying stars on contact; guaranteed once per run from level 2.
detail: G.hyperD = SPB * (longstar ? 24 : 16) and the speed factor is 1+0.9*hv, eased in over 0.35s and out over the last 1.4s, with 1.2s of grace when it ends - so the star never dumps you at double speed into an armed lane. The colour is COL.hyper #ff4fd8, which is why the lesson says pink and not gold. HYPERNOVA is the one name used by the lesson, the say-line, the HUD chip and the lab row.

name: The journey (worlds)
summary: Orbits buy the sky: every completed lap is a seventh of the way to the next world, with a trickle of one world per 150 seconds underneath so nobody is parked.
detail: A reverse banks the travelled arc toward the journey even though it discards the scoring lap, because the comet did cover that distance whichever way it was pointing. A run opens at its level home world and travels outward, so arriving anywhere is earned again each run. The ORBIT lesson names the link once; after that the sky is its own evidence, and there is no instruction channel for the worlds at all.

name: Level record
summary: The deepest level a device has reached moves at death beside the high score, and only for a run that began on level 1 - a picked start can never forge a climb.
detail: G.newLevel = !LAB.on && G.startLevel === 1 && G.level > G.lvlMax. The death screen prints NEW FURTHEST LEVEL, or NEW BEST SCORE, or "Best score  N", or "Practice scores are not saved" in the lab - MECHANICS.md still calls that line FURTHEST YET, which is not a string in the source. The title screen prints BEST and LEVEL n from the same records.

name: Magnet (white/violet horseshoe)
summary: For 10 seconds stars within 110 scale units on the current or an adjacent ring curve into the comet over 0.38s; guaranteed once per run from level 3.
detail: MAGNET_RANGE 110, MAGNET_SECS 10, MAGNET_FLIGHT 0.38; LONG MAGNET extends it to 16s. Collection uses the ordinary star and combo rewards - no tap or star multiplier. The internal keys are still spot and stagelight so existing saves keep working, which is why the orb id and its player-facing name disagree.

name: The Mirror
summary: A second comet opposite you on your own ring for sixteen beats: it gathers what it passes and shatters red on contact, and it does not protect you.
detail: Its angle is derived as G.angle + PI rather than integrated, so it cannot drift and needs no controller - the lesson the magnetar taught twice. It pays at the chain current rate but never advances the combo, because the chain is the measure of the player own hand. Guaranteed once per run from level 4; 24 beats with LONG MIRROR. ECHO is a banned string in check.mjs because a cut orb by that name outlived its teaching data.

values.lesson: Mirror: a second comet collects stars and clears red for about 9s

name: Movement instrument
summary: Taps and swipes keep the same short chord-aware instrument through every musical passage - no input recording, replay mode, melody task or drum remapping.
detail: This is a negative contract as much as a feature: CLAUDE.md forbids any temporary tap-to-play melody, drum or echo assignment, and tryLand() survives as an empty function with the comment "a reward never asks for a different tap". A swipe into a wall still plays its note, which makes it the one input with no survival consequence and therefore the one you can play purely for the music.

name: Music answers you
summary: Turns and ring changes sound as chord tones through the movement instrument; the controls never change job to play the music.
detail: performerHit is called from reverse, hop and the wall-bump path, so every input has a note attached whether or not it was in time. MEET.music - "Each tap and ring change plays a note" - fires on the first reverse and is the only sentence in the game about the musical layer as a whole.

values.lesson: Each tap and ring change plays a note

name: The Narrows
summary: A wall across every ring but one at dl 520 - the mirror of GATES, answered by the hop instead of the tap.
detail: The open lane is always adjacent to the comet and never the ring it is already on, so exactly one swipe answers it, and the lane is held to a wider clearance than the walls because a shard sitting in the only way out turns a demand into a trap. It does not use the gate reverseEscape check: the escape it must guarantee is a lane, not an arc.

values.lesson: Swipe to the ring with no wall

name: Near miss
summary: Stopping just short of a shard on your ring, or sweeping past one on the ring you just left mid-hop, pays +3 and pops DODGED +3.
detail: Only those two shapes count, because a graze has to be a dodge; the saucer is excluded since its body was never going to touch you, and a shard on any other ring earns nothing. The popup is the entire teaching channel - there is no lesson and no hint rung for it.

name: New sounds
summary: The star instrument steps up at the THIRD RING, SHUTTERS and THE EYE rungs, announced once per voice per visit as NEW SOUND: TWIN SYNTHS / SYNTH LEAD / ELECTRIC GUITAR.
detail: T_VOICE is derived from the TIERS table by name rather than by ordinal, because inserting DIVERS and THE NARROWS moved THE EYE from index 10 to 12 and silently re-timed every hardcoded ordinal. SND_SEEN is keyed by voice ordinal 1/2/3, so the two writers - a live tier crossing and a pre-climbed level start - cannot announce the same voice twice. The line waits 3.8s or 4.5s for its banner to clear and defers entirely inside a black hole.

name: Nova (white orb)
summary: One expanding front converts the shards it sweeps into stars, with 0.95s of invulnerability so you cannot die inside your own blast.
detail: The front does the converting through novaConvert, so threats arriving behind it are untouched and expiry adds no invisible clear. RICH NOVA makes each cleared shard leave two stars. Third of the three guaranteed intro placements, named by its hint rung and its say-line.

name: Orbit scoring
summary: A full circle without turning pays 6+13*min(lapEmbers,4) plus a streak bonus of min(7*(streak-1),28), and buys a seventh of the sky journey.
detail: A lap is star-fed when G.lapEmbers>0; only fed laps raise G.lapStreak, and the streak bonus saturates at five laps, for a maximum payout of 86. The ORBIT +N popup only prints on streaks 1-3 and at milestones 3, 5 and every fifth after, so a fast player can orbit all run and never read the word - which is why MEET.orbit fires on the first completed lap instead.

name: Overcharge
summary: While the shield bank is full, stars pay double and a tight tap pays a flat +8; the orbit payout is deliberately not doubled.
detail: The doubling is one clause of the star pickup (G.shields>=shieldMax() adds another G.combo) and one branch of judgeTiming. The say-line reads "Shields full: stars now score double" - not "everything" - and waits behind the red lesson, so an economy nuance cannot be the loudest thing on a first-ever run. cueState marks both the open and the close.

name: Overdrive
summary: Holding the heat above 0.75 for eight beats tips the run into 64 units of double-time where stars and on-beat taps pay double.
detail: Gated on dl > 18, on no drop being in flight, and on a 45-second cooldown, so it is a reward for sustained play rather than a timer. It announces itself with "Double points for stars and on-beat taps", the state shimmer and the gold band, and it is the second of the three states the HUD prints as an x2 chip.

name: Pause
summary: One early return in update() before G.t moves freezes every deadline together; the panel is opaque, RESUME counts in for 3s and pause re-arms 5s after play restarts.
detail: PAUSE is a flag, not a G.state, because draw() dispatches with the death screen as its final else and a paused state would have rendered GAME OVER over a live run. The board is hidden on purpose - a button that freezes a warning mid-flight is a difficulty change wearing a convenience label - and paused time is measured in wall clock, since a backgrounded tab produces no frames at all.

name: Plain shard (red)
summary: Red costs a shield and only kills on an empty bank; it telegraphs first, and all four channels that name it say "costs a shield" rather than "kills".
detail: A hit with shields left spends one, grants 0.9s of invulnerability and pops "-1 SHIELD - N LEFT"; the hit that empties the bank pops "NO SHIELDS: AVOID RED". smoke.mjs fails the build if any MEET string matches /red kills/. The first shard of a run is held until age() reaches firstShardAt(), which is 13s on a first-ever run and 4.5s from the fourth.

values.lesson: Red hits cost a shield; tap to turn or swipe rings

name: POWERUP TESTING (the lab)
summary: A sandbox reached from the title screen that places one chosen orb repeatedly on a board pinned at dl 40, teaches nothing and writes nothing to the device.
detail: LAB_DL is 40 - exactly THIRD RING, the lowest clock value that gives the arena all three orbits, because the black hole opens a fourth on entry. The ghost toggle (red cannot touch you, default on) is read at the single lethal-contact site. Neither firstMeet nor the pickup shortcut may spend a lesson here, and dying in the lab neither spends nor re-arms one.

name: Reverse (tap)
summary: A tap flips the comet instantly, discarding the orbit in progress and the lap streak while every star already collected stays banked.
detail: reverse() zeroes G.lapAcc and G.lapStreak and never touches G.score, and it banks the discarded arc toward the sky journey (G.skyW += (lapAcc/TAU)/ORB_PER_WORLD) so a player who only ever taps still travels. Taught by FIRST FLIGHT step 1, the hint rung "Tap to turn around", the menu demo, and MEET.lapcost on the first reversal that throws away most of a lap. MECHANICS.md also credits a "menu key row", which the title screen no longer draws.

name: Rings
summary: Inner rings are tighter and run a hotter filter (RINGS[].lift 0/380/820), but angular speed and star payout are identical on every ring.
detail: G.angle advances by G.dir*G.speed*sdt with no radius term, so no ring changes how fast you travel; the honest reward for diving is the filter lift you can hear, which is why the THIRD RING banner promises "more stars" rather than the retired "faster and higher". Ring 2 unlocks at dl 12 and ring 3 at dl 40; the black hole opens a fourth on entry and puts it back on the way out.

name: The saucer
summary: The only shape placed against the player: it holds 0.55 rad off your tail, and turning back makes it charge for a beat and block that ring for 0.42s.
detail: Its body is never solid - only the shot is - so there is no contact death and the counter always exists: it is standing on the ring you left, and it takes 0.42s to follow a hop. One at a time on a 9-15s cooldown, and never on a board with a wall, because the gate exists to force a reversal and the saucer exists to price one.

values.lesson: Turning triggers its shot; swipe to another ring

name: Scorch
summary: For 8 seconds the arc of your ring you have already travelled stays lit and destroys any red standing in it, converting it through the nova path.
detail: Stored as 72 sectors per ring rather than a list of arcs - sectors cannot overlap or leak - and painted from the previous angle to the current one, because at 4.2 rad/s a per-frame point sample leaves holes. A full lap makes a full lap safe and standing still makes almost nothing safe, which is the saucer problem answered from the reward side. Guaranteed once per run from level 5; 13s with DEEP BURN.

values.lesson: Scorch: your path clears red obstacles for 8s

name: Shield (green orb)
summary: A banked hit-eater: every run starts with two, the cap is 3 and steps to 4 at dl 160 and 5 at dl 320, and a spend costs nothing but the shield.
detail: shieldMax() is d<160?3:d<320?4:5. DEEP BANK adds a third starting shield rather than raising the cap, because overcharge requires a FULL bank and raising the cap would have made a pure-upside tile quietly cost score. The cap crossing says "You can now hold N shields" and closes the overcharge shimmer, so a bank that silently stopped being full now announces it. Shield is the first of the three guaranteed intro placements.

name: Shutter pairs
summary: A twin whose halves strictly alternate at duty 0.5 offset half a cycle, so exactly one side is solid at every instant; dl 310.
detail: The lesson was the good design and the mechanic moved to meet it: at the lone shutter duty of 0.55 both halves were armed for 10% of every cycle, so a player who waited for the gap died doing exactly what they were told. smoke.mjs walks a full period at 120 samples and fails on a single frame where both or neither is armed. Called FLICKER PAIRS until commit 01a3a25.

values.lesson: The shapes take turns opening; pass through the open one

name: Shutters
summary: A shard that phases on a two-beat cycle at 0.55 duty from dl 165: harmless as an open shutter, lethal as a solid red crystal.
detail: armed() is blinkPhase(s) < BLINK*duty(s), with BLINK = SPB*2 and BDUTY = 0.55, so a lone shutter is lethal for 55% of every two beats. The tier and both its sentences were called BLINKERS - "Pass while dim; bright red costs a shield" - until commit 01a3a25 renamed the object and reworded the lesson to "Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red". tools/curriculum.mjs still names BLINKERS in its banner-order ladder.

values.lesson: Pass through the open shape; avoid solid red

name: Sliding gates
summary: A gate whose wall drifts along the rings at dl 240 - the same reversal, demanded earlier, because the exit is crowding shut.
detail: A compound of gate and drift: the spawn gives every segment the same va of 0.18-0.34 rad/s in one direction. It obeys the gate rules - one wall at a time, never beside a saucer, and vetted for a 1.1 rad reversal - and its lesson names the timing rather than a new verb: tap to turn BEFORE it reaches you.

values.lesson: The wall moves; tap to turn before it reaches you

name: Slipstream
summary: For 12 seconds every successful hop converts non-saucer shards within 0.48 rad of the landing angle into stars on that ring.
detail: The landing carries 0.4s of grace awarded at most once per 0.8s, so chaining swipes clears every time but cannot sustain immunity. A swipe beyond the available rings and the black hole gravity pull do not activate it. Level 2 hop reward, guaranteed once per run behind hypernova; 18s with LONG SLIPSTREAM.

name: Slow-mo (violet orb)
summary: Six seconds at 0.55x simulation time, nine with SLOW WORLD; the second of the three guaranteed intro placements.
detail: The dilation is the tsT term feeding G.tsCur, which scales sdt - so it slows movement, spawn clocks and shard motion together rather than being a separate rule. Named by a hint rung that fires while the orb is still on the board and by the pickup say-line, which prints the real duration rather than the base number.

name: Star dive (the finale)
summary: Every level ends with an eleven-star cadence trail plus a sun that blooms only once the melody is nearly gathered, announced as LEVEL END rather than UNLOCKED.
detail: It latches at dl >= lvEnd-10 with no payoff in flight, clears the board and runs on its own 50-second cap. With no AudioContext there is no duet at all: the level simply completes at its finish line. The eyebrow is LEVEL END because nothing is unlocked here - tier, ring count and spawn pool are untouched by the latch.

name: Star trail
summary: Nine marked gold stars laid out ahead in the direction already travelled, alternating between the current ring and one adjacent, worth four bonus points each.
detail: Each collects normally and advances the combo; the route waits 16 seconds, or 24 with LONG STAR TRAIL, and a new pickup replaces the previous route. The sequence guides a chase without requiring collection in order, and hazards remain. Level 3 route reward, guaranteed once per run behind Magnet.

name: Starfall
summary: Three star-fed orbits - two with EARLY STARFALL - release an automatic reward: red clears, spawns pause and stars pay double for about 9.23 seconds.
detail: build() only counts src === "orbit", so nothing but a completed fed lap charges it, and it is suppressed in the lab, the intro, a black hole, the finale and during a running Starfall. Length is PAYLEN = PAY*(SPB/2) = 32*(60/104)/2 = 9.23s. No input is asked for: taps always turn.

name: Stars (embers)
summary: Gold collectibles that pay the current combo value, feed the orbit payout, and carry the one player-facing word the game uses for the collectible.
detail: A pickup pays (bhInner?2:1)*G.combo plus 4 for a marked star-trail star, and pays the combo again under Starfall, overdrive, hypernova or a full shield bank. It increments G.lapEmbers, which is what the orbit payout scales on. No lesson names the plain star: it is taught by the menu demo, the intro step "Collect the star" and the combo lesson.

name: THE EYE
summary: The last rung of the tier ladder at dl 610 carries type:null - it adds no shape and no ring, and exists to mark the end of teaching.
detail: Its dl 610 boundary coincides with level 6 opening, and smoke.mjs pins the last tier at the last level floor so nothing can be appended past it. It was called STORM until that collided with LV[2].name and printed LEVEL 4 - STORM over a card that said EVENT HORIZON. Its only channel is the banner name; the sub can render only if the crossing escapes the endgame suppression window.

values.sub: Collect stars and complete orbits to score

name: Timing (the groove chain)
summary: A movement landing inside the timing window climbs an eight-step chain that colours the movement instrument and pays only on the way up.
detail: judgeTiming returns 0 with no AudioContext, so every timing reward is audio-only by design and the game is honest with sound off. The window is TIGHT, or 0.045s with STEADY HAND; a sixteenth-accurate but off-quarter hit HOLDS the chain and refreshes its 2.8s decay rather than climbing. The chain pays its own index on each climb and nothing for holding, never charges Starfall and never changes what a gesture does.

name: Twin shards
summary: Two shards on one ring at dl 18, wide enough that the answer is a ring change rather than a late reverse; the tier is held until the first hop lands.
detail: tierIndex() clamps the ladder to SECOND RING while G.didHop is false on level 1, with a 30 difficulty-second release valve, so the tier that makes hopping compulsory can never arrive before the gesture has been used once. Taught by the TWIN SHARDS banner, MEET.twin and the death coach - twins stamp their pairing on both shards so a twin death coaches the hop rather than reporting a plain single.

values.lesson: Two red obstacles: swipe to another ring

name: Upgrade draft
summary: Three of eleven upgrade tiles are offered on each level card; taken tiles never repeat and declined ones return only once the fresh pool runs thin.
detail: rollOffer() filters on (minLevel||1) <= G.level+1 and !G.upg[id], so LONG SLIPSTREAM enters at the level-2 card and LONG STAR TRAIL at level 3. Only a real advance rolls an offer - a retry re-reads the same card and hands out nothing. check.mjs fails the build if an offered id has no upgOn() reader, which is how nine tiles that changed nothing were caught.

name: Which orbs have sprite art
summary: Nine of the ten orbs map to a power-*.webp texture; `spot` (Magnet) is absent from artKey by design and always draws its procedural horseshoe crystal.
detail: artifactSprite bakes a sprite at the current scale from host.getTexture(artKey) when present and falls back to the faceted crystal plus artifactGlyph otherwise. docs/art/catalog.json marks power-spotlight.webp 'Retired Spotlight art; not the current Magnet. Do not map to runtime spot.' -- yet it is still in public/art/manifest.json and BootScene loads every manifest texture, so 25.7KB of retired art is fetched and decoded on every boot for a key nothing reads. drawPow routes everything except the black hole to artifactPower; the black hole keeps a hand-drawn fallback used only when its texture is absent.

name: THE BASS BOMB (removed)
summary: Cut by the owner because its whole identity lived in the audio channel: with sound off it was a weaker nova over a never-drawn wedge, and LONG FUSE widened an invisible number.
detail: Its visual tell -- a subwoofer cone slamming on the beat -- rode G.beat, which only moves when the audio scheduler feeds it, so for a muted player the sprite sat motionless and the pickup was a cyan flash. What remained was the same novaConvert pipeline over a +/-60 degree wedge instead of the whole board, without invulnerability, at the same rotation odds. Two orbs occupying one job, one of them inferior and illegible, is one orb too many. Its 0.15 share was redistributed proportionally, which is the standing rule for a removal.

name: Ordinary rewards suspend inside a black hole
summary: updateOrbMotion returns immediately while bhActive(), so mirror, scorch, slipstream, magnet attraction, route lifetimes and Starfall consume no time inside the mode.
detail: Remaining reward time resumes after the closing warp. The ember loop skips trail, mag and starfall stars entirely while bhActive() and ages them on rewardDt otherwise. updateMagnetStar returns early too, so a captured star freezes mid-flight rather than finishing into a comet the mode has moved. No orb spawns during the mode at all -- an orb in here is either a lifeline undoing the difficulty the mode exists to create, or a musical orb whose effect is on an arrangement that is halted.

name: BLACK HOLE
summary: The one optional, dangerous orb: a 17-second mode on a temporary fourth ring, guaranteed to be OFFERED once on level 4 and otherwise a 5% roll from level 3.
detail: Phases: 0 off, 1 opening (BH_WARP 0.85s), 2 challenge, 3 closing. Ring zero is OUTERMOST throughout. The escape signal opens at BH_ESCAPE and the deadline is BH_DUR. Motion runs at BH_TS after the warp; density climbs from 1.25 to 2 across the pre-escape window; gravity pulls one ring inward every BH_PULL seconds until escape opens. Placement arms bhCool = t+20 (the decline price); actually taking it arms t+55 on the event. Its MEET lesson is the only orb lesson that is NOT soft, because taking it starts a mode rather than granting a gift.

name: The black hole's cash-out
summary: Escaping pays round((80 + 600*charge + 20*stars) / 1.5^min(3,shieldsSpent)); missing the deadline costs the bank and one shield, or ends an unshielded run.
detail: charge accrues at dt/8 only while settled on the innermost ring before escape opens, so eight seconds of inner-ring travel fills it; entry alone awards nothing. BH.score counts stars collected during phase 2. shieldsSpent is measured as G.blocks minus the count at entry, so the divisor prices being saved during the mode. Inner-ring stars pay double during phase 2 -- and that bonus was on the WRONG ring once, because index 0 is the outermost orbit.

name: Orb spawn cadence and lifetime
summary: One orb on the board at a time, never during the finale, Starfall or a black hole; it lives 7 seconds and the next arms at max(6, rand(10,15) - dl*0.02).
detail: A run opens with powT = 4 which, with the dl()>=6 gate, puts the first shield on the board around ten seconds in. A failed placement retries in 0.5s. In the lab the refill is rand(2.2, 3.6) instead, bought entirely on the refill so the one-orb-at-a-time gate is preserved -- two on the board at once is not a thing the real game ever does, and a rig that shows an arrangement the game cannot produce is testing the wrong object.

name: What the harnesses assert about orbs
summary: Six orbs have their pickup effect asserted in smoke.mjs; shield, hypernova and the black hole have none, and nothing anywhere reads sinceShield, POWPOOL or overcharge.
detail: smoke.mjs calls pickup() for warp, slip, trail, mirror, scorch and spot only; nova is exercised through a direct novaBlast call and the black hole through startBlackHole. Its lab sweep plays every LAB_ORBS row for 45 seconds and requires at least two placements of that type and no other, which is the broadest placement guarantee in the suite and grows with the roster for free. fxcheck proves all eight non-shield orb kinds can own a visible scene event. curriculum requires a reachable lesson for the six musical orbs and the level-2/level-3 guarantee pairs.

name: ECHO and METEOR -- banned teaching keys
summary: check.mjs fails the build only when MEET or teachSoft references 'echo' or 'meteor'; the docs overstate this as a banned string, and both words appear elsewhere freely.
detail: The guard is a regex over (MEET= or teachSoft=) followed by the quoted id, so it catches teaching data outliving a cut orb and nothing else. ECHO was the runner-up name for THE MIRROR, which was called THE TWIN as a working name and renamed because TWIN SHARDS is a formation met at dl 18. METEOR is a second cut orb whose name survives nowhere else in the design record.

name: The once-per-RUN guarantee flags
summary: hyperPlaced, spotPlaced, mirrorPlaced, scorchPlaced, slipPlaced and trailPlaced survive level boundaries and start pre-spent for every home level a run opens past.
detail: startGame() re-arms them only when the run is not carrying a score forward, and even then sets each to (G.level > homeLevel). So a 1->6 climb meets each orb exactly once on its home level, and a REDSHIFT start is not owed four marquee placements in its first minute. Re-arming at every boundary was a real shipped bug: one measured climb guaranteed HYPERNOVA on L2, L3, L4, L5 and L6 and buried level 5's own two introductions. bhPlaced is different -- it is cleared by every startGame, and bhRun is the flag that survives.

name: The timed-reward HUD rows
summary: drawPowerStatus draws one row per live timed reward -- name, ceil(seconds)+'s' and a progress bar -- and returns immediately during a black hole or the intro.
detail: Rows are Hypernova, Magnet, Mirror, Scorch, Slipstream, Slow-mo and Star trail. Star trail's countdown is derived from any live s.trail star's remaining life rather than a separate timer. On a wide viewport the list sits in the right margin beside the arena; otherwise it stacks under the header in up to two columns. Magnet is drawn in COL.comet here while its arc flash is COL.warp and its pickup burst is #eaf1ff -- three different colours for one orb, and it shares the cyan with Slipstream on the same list.

name: HYPERNOVA (id `hyper`)
summary: Magenta orb, level 2's guarantee: sixteen beats (9.231s) of invincibility at up to +90% speed, converting every red you plow through into a paying ember.
detail: G.hyperD = SPB * (LONGER STAR ? 24 : 16). Speed is speedAt()*(1+0.9*hv) where hv = min(1, (hyperD-hyper)/0.35, hyper/1.4) -- a 0.35s ease in, a 1.4s ease out, so the star never dumps you at double speed into an armed lane; expiry then grants G.t+1.2 of grace. Armed red met while it burns is routed to novaConvert ahead of the shield branch. Stars pay double while it burns and a tight tap pays a flat +8; the orbit payout, as everywhere, is untouched. Named HYPERNOVA in every channel after shipping as 'the pink star' in one.

name: The HYPERNOVA x2 chip does not exist
summary: MECHANICS.md and powerups.md both describe a standing 'HYPERNOVA x2' HUD chip; the code draws a named seconds countdown and the string appears nowhere in runtime.js.
detail: drawPowerStatus builds rows of [label, remaining, duration, colour] -- Hypernova, Magnet, Mirror, Scorch, Slipstream, Slow-mo, Star trail -- each drawn as a name, ceil(seconds)+'s' and a progress bar. No multiplier chip exists for any orb. The only NOUN x N examples in the file are in the house-style comment that defines the idiom. SPOTLIGHT x2 is the same case one orb along.

name: STARRUN -- the hypernova's tune
summary: Sixteen sixteenths of pentatonic degrees 4-10 that climb and wrap, restated every bar over an eighth-note bass, added as an overlay rather than a third section.
detail: STARRUN is [4,5,6,7, 5,6,7,8, 6,7,8,9, 7,8,9,10] -- four ascending four-note cells each starting a degree higher, so the line spirals and never resolves. It is an overlay because a section change can only land at a four-bar seam, which can be most of a loop away against a star that lasts four bars; applySect is the only writer of CH/ARP and a mid-bar harmony swap would break the rule the payoff, rise, black hole and star dive exceptions exist to protect. Written as degrees so it transposes with the level key, and it sits above the band's degree-4 arp ceiling. powerColour returns immediately while G.hyper>0, so the mirror and scorch voices yield to it; a black hole outranks it.

name: The hypernova's comet tail
summary: A hypernova widens the ribbon 1.85x, crossfades its three passes to the orb's magenta and gold, doubles the particle ceiling and sheds sparks without a groove chain.
detail: Everything rides G.hyperGlow rather than G.hyper, so it arrives and leaves with the corona instead of snapping with the timer; at hyperGlow 0 the arithmetic reduces to the ordinary ribbon. Half-width gains (1+0.85*hyperGlow), trailCap climbs 62 -> 110 samples, the wake ceiling goes 80 -> 160 particles and the spawn interval is divided by up to 3.2. DRIFT WORTH KNOWING: MECHANICS.md and powerups.md both say the star draws 'five passes instead of three'. As of commit 01a3a25 the pass table holds three entries (two when ghosted) and the star is expressed as an hmix colour crossfade on those three, not as extra passes.

name: POWERUP TESTING (the lab)
summary: A sandbox that places one chosen orb every ~3 seconds on a board pinned at dl 40, bypassing the intro trio, level floors, guarantees, shield pity and the black hole's rarity.
detail: LAB.on short-circuits spawnPow's first branch. LAB_DL is 40 -- exactly TIERS[3].at, the lowest clock value that gives the arena all three orbits, because the black hole opens a FOURTH on entry and a one-ring lab would demonstrate that against nothing. The ghost (red cannot touch you, on by default) is read at the single lethal-contact site ahead of the hypernova and shield branches, so nothing downstream fires. Nothing a lab session does reaches the device: no record, no run count, no lesson, no preference, and only one telemetry event. The LAB literal carries type:'blackhole', but enterPowerSel immediately overwrites it from LAB.sel, so the orb actually armed on a fresh visit is LAB_ORBS[5] -- the mirror.

name: The ledger-drift guard, and what it cannot see
summary: check.mjs fails the build if any TIERS name or LAB_ORBS name is absent from MECHANICS.md; it is a lowercase substring test, one-directional, and it never reads UPG.
detail: All ten LAB_ORBS names and all eleven UPG names appear in MECHANICS.md today, and every orb has a real row or section rather than an incidental mention -- so the rule is currently satisfied. What the guard cannot catch: a ledger row describing behaviour the code no longer has (the HYPERNOVA x2 chip), a row filed under the wrong heading (Magnet sits in the level-2 table while its own cell says level 3), a twelfth upgrade tile, or an orb added to spawnPow but never to LAB_ORBS. The names.length<8 floor exists because a regex that stops matching yields an empty list and an empty loop reports success.

name: POW_LESSON and the guarantee that is of the INTRODUCTION
summary: An unseen musical orb that expires unlessoned clears its own placed flag, so the guarantee is of the lesson landing rather than of one spawn roll.
detail: POW_LESSON maps orb id -> guarantee flag for spot, hyper, mirror, scorch, slip, trail and blackhole. firstMeet is called at placement AND re-offered every frame the orb is still on the board, because the single call at placement can hit a busy moment and defer. Two writers spend a lesson, not one: firstMeet fires the sentence, and the pickup path separately treats TAKING a musical orb as having been taught it -- both are guarded against the lab, and the harness found the second.

name: MAGNET (id `spot`)
summary: Level 3's guarantee: for 10 seconds stars within 110 scale units on the current or an adjacent ring curve into the moving comet over a 0.38s flight.
detail: Captures stars only -- never shards -- gated on Math.abs(s.ring-effRing())<=1 and a distance test against MAGNET_RANGE. Each capture builds a quadratic Bezier whose control point is bent min(22, d*0.28) perpendicular to the line of flight and extends the star's own life so it survives the trip. starVisualPos is authoritative for contact, crystal, bloom and route links. updateMagnetStar returns immediately while bhActive(), so both attraction and captured-star lifetimes freeze inside a black hole. There is no star or tap multiplier and no temporary instrument mode.

name: THE MAGNETAR (removed)
summary: Died twice proving a first-order chase never arrives on a circular board, which is why THE MIRROR derives its angle instead of integrating one.
detail: It is also why check.mjs forbids any second radius on an ember or an orb: the magnetar gave embers a free radius in s.pr so they could curve between rings, the bloom pass never read it, and sixteen glows sat detached from their embers by up to 89px on a 390px screen. The guard is inverted deliberately -- rather than police two radii staying in sync, it fails if a second radius is assigned at all. Its 0.11 share was redistributed proportionally.

name: The seven orb MEET lessons
summary: Six reward orbs carry soft:1 first-encounter sentences (no time dilation); the black hole's is deliberately hard, because taking it starts a mode rather than granting a gift.
detail: Shield, slow-mo and nova have no MEET row: they are taught by the level-1 card, the hint ladder and their own say() line at pickup. A hard lesson additionally refuses to fire while any timed reward is live (hyper, spot, slow, mirror, scorch, slip or a live route), because 2.8 frozen seconds is a third of the marquee item burned while the player cannot move. smoke.mjs only asserts the soft flag for spot, hyper and lapcost -- mirror, scorch, slip and trail could lose it silently.

values.spot: Magnet: nearby stars curve into you for 10 seconds
values.hyper: Hypernova: move faster, safe from red, for about 9s
values.mirror: Mirror: a second comet collects stars and clears red for about 9s
values.scorch: Scorch: your path clears red obstacles for 8s
values.slip: Slipstream: swipe rings to clear nearby red for 12s
values.trail: Star trail: collect nine bonus stars within 16s
values.blackhole: Black hole: ride the inner ring; at ESCAPE, swipe to the outer ring

name: THE MIRROR
summary: Level 4's guarantee: a second comet at G.angle+PI on your own ring for sixteen beats that gathers stars and shatters armed red, pays, but never advances the combo.
detail: Its angle is DERIVED every frame, never integrated -- a chaser that accumulates its own position drifts and needs a controller, and the magnetar died twice proving a first-order chase never arrives. Contact uses the same swept arc the player's pickup check uses and stays on the old ring through the first half of a hop. It skips st.trail and st.mag stars: the offered route and a star already flying to the player belong to the player. It pays max(1, G.combo) and leaves the chain where it found it. It cannot be hurt and it does not protect you.

name: NOVA
summary: White orb: one expanding front converts the shards present at pickup into reachable stars on the player's own ring, with 0.95s of grace covering the sweep.
detail: Home level 1, third of the POW_INTRO trio, and the only pickup branch that names no type -- it is the final else of the chain, which is why a static 'one branch per orb id' scan cannot find it. novaBlast snapshots G.spikes into targets, so threats spawning after the blast are never erased; the front's own expiry converts nothing. Speed is max(560*u, (2R+60u)/0.62) so a wide viewport still clears the ring system inside the grace.

name: novaConvert -- the shared red-to-star path
summary: One function turns an armed shard into collectable embers on the player's ring, and five separate rewards route through it: nova, hypernova, mirror, scorch and slipstream.
detail: The ember lands on the ring the PLAYER is on (or an explicit toRing, which only slipstream passes) at the shard's angle, stepping 0.36 rad in the travel direction up to 8 times until it has 0.30 rad of clearance -- so a converted wall reads as a necklace, never a pile. RICH NOVA emits two and both walk that same spacing search. Each conversion also takes the next sixteenth slot and the next pentatonic degree, so a cascade plays a strict ascending run; a gap of more than 0.8s restarts the run from the bottom.

name: Overcharge (full shield bank)
summary: While the shield bank is full, embers pay double and a tight tap pays a flat +8; an overflow shield pays +50, and the orbit payout is untouched.
detail: Not an orb: a state the shield orb opens. G.shields>=shieldMax() is one arm of the standing-state doubling branch alongside overdrive and hypernova, and one arm of the flat +8 tight-tap branch. The announcement 'Shields full: stars now score double' waits for G.seen.single so the red lesson lands first; cueState(true) opens the shimmer either way. shieldMax() stepping 3->4->5 at dl 160/320 silently ends a full bank, which is why BANK DEEPER exists.

name: Where an orb may be placed
summary: Up to 24 tries at a random angle and ring, each accepted only if farFromAll(a, ring, 0.6, sep(ring,3.2), sep(ring,3.0)) clears it of the player, stars and shards.
detail: Rewards keep the OLD symmetric player clearance rather than the heading-aware bubble the hazard pass uses: letting stars and orbs fill in behind a stationary player would hand the camper a reason to stay, which is the behaviour the asymmetric rule exists to price. If all 24 attempts fail, spawnPow returns false, no flag is spent and powT is set to 0.5 for a quick retry.

name: POWPOOL -- the fallback weights
summary: The nine-row [id, weight, minLevel] table behind the guarantees; weights sum to 1.190 and are renormalised over the rows the current level unlocks.
detail: The first seven rows sum to exactly 1.000 -- the roster before SLIPSTREAM and STAR TRAIL, which were appended at 0.095 each rather than taken out of the existing space. ptot is recomputed over eligible rows every call, so what a player sees is weight/ptot: at level 1 that is 47.9/29.4/22.7 for shield/warp/nova, and at level 5-6 it is 25.4/15.5/12.0/11.3/6.4/6.7/6.7/8.0/8.0 across all nine. blackhole is NOT in the table; it arrives only from its own two branches. Nothing outside runtime.js reads POWPOOL.

name: The orb roster
summary: Ten selectable orbs ship, listed in LAB_ORBS; three ids do not match their on-screen names (warp=SLOW-MO, spot=MAGNET, hyper=HYPERNOVA).
detail: LAB_ORBS is the roster of record: tools/check.mjs compares its n: names against MECHANICS.md, and smoke.mjs derives its lab sweep from it. An orb added to spawnPow but not to LAB_ORBS is invisible to both. The id drift is save compatibility, not sloppiness -- spot/spotPlaced/spotGlow/stagelight survive the Spotlight-to-Magnet redesign so existing G.upg and preference keys keep working.

name: SCORCH
summary: Level 5's guarantee: for 8 seconds the arc of your own ring you have travelled stays lit and destroys any red standing in or arming into it.
detail: A full lap makes a full lap safe; sitting still makes almost nothing safe -- that asymmetry is the design, and it is the saucer's camping problem answered from the reward side. Stored as 72 sectors per ring in a Float32Array (four rings allocated once per run) because sectors cannot overlap or leak. Painted from G.prevAngle to the current angle in ceil(sweep/step) samples, so nothing is skipped at 4.2 rad/s. Sector lifetime is max(BURN_LIFE, TAU/max(0.3,G.speed)+0.2) in GAMEPLAY seconds, so slow motion preserves the wake. Drawn under the shards. Warm orange, deliberately not warm red.

name: SHIELD
summary: Green banked orb: one hit each, spent automatically for 0.9s of invulnerability; cap is 3/4/5 by difficulty clock and every run starts with two.
detail: Home level 1, first of the POW_INTRO trio (shield -> slow-mo -> nova), placed once per RUN on G.introN. A hit spends one, sets G.invuln=G.t+0.9 and knocks you off the orbit but deliberately does NOT clear lapAcc or lapStreak. Picking one up at a full bank pays a flat +50 instead of banking. Drawn from power-shield.webp when the texture is present, otherwise a mint faceted crystal with a cross-in-shield glyph.

name: The shield-pity rule
summary: Three placements without a shield forces the next one to be a shield, and the branch sits above the black hole so an optional event can never postpone survival.
detail: G.sinceShield counts PLACEMENTS, not pickups -- otherwise a run spent dodging would serve nothing but shields forever. It resets to 0 on a shield and increments on everything else. A pity shield placed while the intro trio still owes one also advances G.introN, because the thing the slot exists to show has just been shown. No harness anywhere reads sinceShield.

name: SLIPSTREAM (id `slip`)
summary: Level 2's second guarantee: for 12 seconds each successful hop converts non-saucer shards within 0.48 rad of the landing angle into stars on that destination ring.
detail: It fires inside hop() AFTER the ring index is committed, so only a successful player hop counts: an invalid swipe returns before that point and black-hole gravity moves G.ringI directly in bhTick without calling hop(). The clear happens on every valid hop, but the 0.4s landing grace is metered by G.slipAt at most once per 0.8s, so chained swipes cannot become continuous immunity. Saucers are exempt from the clear. It is the only one of novaConvert's five call sites that passes an explicit destination ring.

name: SLOW-MO (id `warp`)
summary: Violet orb: six seconds at 55% speed, nine with SLOW WORLD; the dilation rides G.tsCur so the whole visible world slows, not just the simulation.
detail: Home level 1, second of the POW_INTRO trio. The pickup sets G.slow and G.slowD and says 'Slow-mo: movement slows for Ns'. The target timescale tsT is 0.55 while G.slow>0 (a black hole outranks it at BH_TS 0.60, or 0.372 during the opening warp) and G.tsCur eases toward it asymmetrically -- 3.2/s going down, 8/s coming back. Sprite key is power-slow, not power-warp.

name: spawnPow's branch ladder
summary: A single if/else chain decides every placement: lab, intro trio, shield pity, black hole, then the six guarantees, then the weighted POWPOOL roll.
detail: Order is the design: an earlier branch always wins. The two black-hole branches sit directly below the intro trio and above every guarantee, deliberately -- the guarantee flags are patient and survive a delayed placement, while an unrolled per-placement die is simply gone. Note that the mirror (level 4) is tested before Magnet (level 3), so a run that reaches level 4 with spotPlaced still false is handed the mirror first. The pity shield outranks every optional offer, including the black hole.

name: SPOTLIGHT (replaced by MAGNET)
summary: Not removed but redesigned in place after the owner found its stage metaphor confusing; its ids (spot, spotPlaced, spotGlow, stagelight) all survive for save compatibility.
detail: The review that killed it found its active state changed ZERO arena pixels for its whole nine-to-fourteen seconds: the entire inventory was an audio mix move (instrument x1.5, pad to 0.8) plus a text chip that only drew on tall viewports, and its one universal effect -- stars paying double -- printed the UNDOUBLED number in its popup. Fixing that popup lie repaired the same bug for overdrive, hypernova and overcharge, all of which were adding 2x while printing 1x. Its art still ships and is still loaded; nothing reads it.

name: STAR TRAIL (id `trail`)
summary: Level 3's second guarantee: nine marked gold stars laid 0.62 rad apart ahead in the current direction, alternating two rings, each paying the combo plus four bonus points.
detail: layStarTrail filters out every existing trail star first, so a later pickup replaces the route rather than stacking. Stars sit at G.angle + dir*(0.62 + i*0.62); odd indices go to the adjacent ring (inward if the comet is on the innermost, outward otherwise). Each collects through the ordinary swept-contact path, advances the combo, and adds STAR_ROUTE_BONUS on top. Red stays on the board, so following the route is an active choice, and collecting in order is an invitation rather than a rule. The mirror deliberately leaves route stars for the player.

name: Starfall
summary: Not a spawned orb: the payout for three star-fed orbits (two with EARLY STARFALL), released automatically on the next musical quarter, never asking for a different tap.
detail: build(amount,src) is the only charge entry point and discards everything that is not src==='orbit' with amount>=0.04, so time, embers, hops, taps and near-miss grazes contribute nothing. On the qualifying orbit armDrop schedules the release on the grid when WebAudio is live; with no audio startStarfall fires immediately. The release opens with novaBlast from the arena centre, clearing the board, and holds G.invuln at t+left+0.6 for the whole window. DROP_STEP and DROP_STEP_MAX are both 0 -- the escalating-cost curve the long comment above them describes is retired.

name: Starfall's three waves and its doubling
summary: Three waves of five stars arrive at 0, 3.077 and 6.154 seconds of the 9.231-second window, and each collected star adds its combo value a second time.
detail: starfallWave pushes five stars per wave (capped at 30 stars on the board) at G.angle + dir*(0.55 + j*0.42); every third one (j%3===2) goes to the adjacent ring -- inward if the comet is on the innermost, outward otherwise. Each lives 5 seconds and carries starfall:true. Outside reduced-motion each also carries a `flight` arc thrown in from the level's planet, staggered delay j*0.065 over a duration 0.68+j*0.045, and it is uncollectable until its delay elapses. tickStarfall schedules the next wave every PAYLEN/3. The doubling is an if/else against the standing-state doubling, so hypernova/overdrive/full-bank never stack with it; G.secMult is always 1 today, so that multiply is a no-op left from the retired perfect-landing rule.

name: Only five of eleven tiles have their effect asserted
summary: check.mjs proves every tile id has a live upgOn() call site; only slowworld, stagelight, longslip, longtrail and hairtrig are proved to change anything.
detail: The wiring guard matches against a comment-stripped copy of the source and has been blind twice: an id-after-name row was invisible to the old regex, and a call site surviving only inside a block comment satisfied the old test. It cannot tell a correct effect from an inverted one. Unasserted: longstar, deepbank, richnova, longmirror, deepburn and steadyhand -- which includes both duration tiles for the two newest orbs and the only tile that touches an input.

name: DEEP BANK
summary: Adds one to the starting shield bank -- 2 becomes 3 -- additively with the difficulty mode's own shields knob.
detail: Tile id `deepbank`, colour #7bffc8. G.shields = 2 + (upgOn('deepbank')?1:0) + MD().shields, so it literally means 'one more shield' in either mode. Unasserted by any harness.

name: DEEP BURN
summary: Extends scorch's active paint time from 8 seconds to 13; the wake's own per-sector lifetime is unchanged.
detail: Tile id `deepburn`, colour #ff8a2b. It lengthens how long new wake is laid, not how long a laid sector burns -- that stays max(2.6, one orbit at the current speed). Unasserted by any harness.

name: The upgrade draft
summary: Three of eleven tiles are offered at each of the five level-complete cards; there is no currency, the cost is the choice, and a taken tile never returns.
detail: levelComplete() calls rollOffer() when G.level+1 <= LEVEL_MAX and tapping a tile is the only way past the card. available(x) is (x.minLevel||1) <= G.level+1 && !G.upg[x.id] -- the level being OFFERED, not the one just finished. TAKEN tiles are gone for the run; DECLINED tiles (G.offered) come back only once the fresh pool runs thin, which is the fix for a real bug: the old filter burned every tile it had ever offered, and five draws x three slots against nine tiles left the level-5 and level-6 cards drawing from an empty pool. startLab() clears G.upg, G.offered, G.offer and G.picks.

name: EARLY STARFALL
summary: Drops Starfall from three star-fed orbits to two; the id says nothing about what it does.
detail: Tile id `hairtrig` (docs/design/teaching.md still calls it HAIR TRIGGER). dropNeed() returns 2 with it and 3 without. dropcheck asserts both values.

name: Two tile ids do not say what they do
summary: `hairtrig` is EARLY STARFALL and `stagelight` is LONG MAGNET; both ids were kept so saved G.upg keys survive their tiles being renamed.
detail: docs/design/teaching.md's wiring table still names HAIR TRIGGER and STAGE LIGHT; the shipped tiles print EARLY STARFALL and LONG MAGNET. Ids are unchanged, so check.mjs's wiring guard still passes and MECHANICS.md carries the current names. Grepping a display name finds nothing -- this is the same trap as warp/spot/hyper on the orb side.

name: LONG FUSE (removed)
summary: The bass bomb's duration tile, cut with the orb it upgraded; it had been widening a clear region that was never drawn.
detail: Its removal left seven tiles; LONG MIRROR and DEEP BURN later brought that to nine, and LONG SLIPSTREAM and LONG STAR TRAIL to eleven. The lesson worth keeping is the one the review stated: an upgrade to an effect the player cannot see is an upgrade to nothing, and the tile made that visible before the orb's own illegibility was diagnosed.

name: LONG MIRROR
summary: Extends the mirror from 16 beats (9.231s) to 24 beats (13.846s); the tile prints 'about 14 seconds'.
detail: Tile id `longmirror`, colour #4d8cff. Read once, at the mirror pickup. Unasserted by any harness.

name: LONG SLIPSTREAM
summary: Extends slipstream from 12 seconds to 18; carries minLevel 2 so it is never offered before the orb exists.
detail: Tile id `longslip`, colour #5df0ff, minLevel 2 -- one of only two tiles with a floor. It first appears on the level-2 card. Asserted in smoke.mjs: G.slip === 18.

name: LONGER STAR
summary: Extends the hypernova from 16 beats (9.231s) to 24 beats (13.846s); the tile prints 'about 14 seconds'.
detail: Tile id `longstar`, colour #ff4fd8. Read once, at the hypernova pickup: G.hyperD = SPB*(upgOn('longstar')?24:16). Nothing in tools/ ever sets it, so the effect is unasserted.

name: LONG STAR TRAIL
summary: Extends a star-trail route's life from 16 seconds to 24; carries minLevel 3 so it is never offered before the orb exists.
detail: Tile id `longtrail`, colour #ffc857, minLevel 3. Read in layStarTrail, so it applies to the route laid at pickup rather than to the orb's state. Asserted in smoke.mjs: every new route star carries life 24.

name: RICH NOVA
summary: Each converted red leaves two stars instead of one, and the second walks the same spacing search so a doubled wall is a longer necklace.
detail: Tile id `richnova`, colour #ffffff. Read inside novaConvert, so it also doubles the yield of hypernova, mirror, scorch and slipstream conversions -- not just the nova's. Unasserted by any harness.

name: SLOW WORLD
summary: Extends slow-mo from 6 seconds to 9.
detail: Tile id `slowworld`, colour #b48bff. Asserted in smoke.mjs by taking the orb again with the flag set and reading G.slow === 9.

name: LONG MAGNET
summary: Extends the Magnet field from 10 seconds to 16; the id is the retired Spotlight's, kept so saved G.upg keys survive.
detail: Tile id `stagelight`, colour #b48bff. Asserted in smoke.mjs: take the orb with the flag set and read G.spot === 16.

name: STEADY HAND
summary: Widens the tight-tap timing window from 0.032s to 0.045s -- the only tile that touches an input rather than a reward.
detail: Tile id `steadyhand`, colour #ffc857. Read in judgeTiming as W = upgOn('steadyhand')?0.045:TIGHT, where TIGHT is 0.032. Unasserted by any harness, and it is the tile whose inversion would be hardest to notice.
